title: AI-credit reservation leak in the single-file AI-upload path — `reserve()` is called outside any try/catch, so a downstream throw in `Evidence.create`/`debugLog`/`assignEvidenceCode` never commits or cancels the reservation
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/evidence/evidence-upload.controller.js` — `uploadAI` handler (single-file AI-assisted upload, `POST /upload/ai`)
**Root Cause (original):** `aiUploadBilling.reserve(...)` was called outside any try/catch, and `Evidence.create`/`debugLog`/`assignEvidenceCode` were also unwrapped — inconsistent with the bulk-upload path (`uploadAIBulk`), which already wrapped the equivalent block with `cancelFailed` in the catch.
**Status:** FIXED — re-verified 2026-08-30 after pulling latest `vibrantix-backend` (`feature/dev`, fast-forwarded 9bc7ed00→8641818). `Evidence.create`/`debugLog`/`assignEvidenceCode`/`queueUploadJobs`/`commitSuccessful` now all share one try/catch (lines 799-901), with `aiUploadBilling.cancelFailed(aiCreditReservationId)` in the catch, explicitly mirroring `uploadAIBulk`'s pattern (inline comment cites EM-040 by name). Traced the full handler; the fix is correct and complete — no regression found.
fixEvidence: `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/evidence/evidence-upload.controller.js:793-901` — single try/catch wrapping `Evidence.create` through `commitSuccessful`, with `cancelFailed(aiCreditReservationId)` in the catch and an inline comment explicitly citing EM-040. Confirmed on 2026-08-30 after pulling the latest `feature/dev` (backend HEAD now 8641818).

title: Presigned-upload confirm path bypasses magic-byte content validation — declared `mimeType` is trusted with no inspection of the actual uploaded S3 object bytes, unlike the direct multipart upload path
description:
**Files:** `evidence-upload.controller.js` (`confirmPresignedUpload`); `evidence-upload.multer.js` (`detectDisallowedMagicBytes`); `s3-file-storage.js` (`getFileHeadBytes`)
**Root Cause (original):** The presigned-upload flow validated only the client-declared `mimeType` before issuing the URL, then `confirmPresignedUpload` verified file SIZE via an S3 HEAD request but never downloaded or inspected the object's actual bytes — unlike the direct multer path's `validateMagicBytes` middleware.
**Status:** FIXED — re-verified 2026-08-30 after pulling latest `vibrantix-backend` (`feature/dev`, fast-forwarded 9bc7ed00→8641818). `confirmPresignedUpload` (lines 1822-1902) now, after the existing size check, calls `S3.getFileHeadBytes(s3Key, bucket)` (a new static method on the S3 integration, default 4099-byte range) and runs the bytes through `detectDisallowedMagicBytes` — the SAME detector `evidence-upload.multer.js` exports and uses for the multer path (refactored into one reusable, exported function per the original fix prompt's suggestion #3, not duplicated). A disallowed detected type deletes the S3 object + cancels the storage reservation and returns 400, mirroring the existing size-mismatch rejection path. Verified both helper functions are real (not broken references) and properly wired. No regression found.
fixEvidence: `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/evidence/evidence-upload.controller.js:1850-1861` (magic-byte check inline in `confirmPresignedUpload`, calling `S3.getFileHeadBytes` + `detectDisallowedMagicBytes`) + `evidence-upload.multer.js:97,137` (`detectDisallowedMagicBytes` extracted as a reusable exported function) + `s3-file-storage.js:171` (`getFileHeadBytes` static method) — all confirmed present and correctly wired on 2026-08-30 after pulling the latest `feature/dev` (backend HEAD now 8641818).

description:

title: Google Drive Bearer token sent directly to connector service origin — JWT from `state.auth.token` in raw `fetch()` to `CS_URL` in `GDriveFileBrowser.jsx`; bypasses Next.js API proxy; CORS failure likely in production; violates A.8.20
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/services/integrationHubService.js:10-13` (`CONNECTOR_SERVICE_URL`), `:29-47` (`getIntegrationHubAccessToken`), `:52-69` (axios instance + request interceptor)
**Root Cause:** The implementation has changed but the underlying defect persists in a different location. `GDriveFileBrowser.jsx` itself no longer makes a raw `fetch()` call (confirmed — zero `fetch(` occurrences); it now delegates to `getConnectors`/`getDriveFiles` from `integrationHubService.js`. That service still calls the connector-service origin DIRECTLY (`CONNECTOR_SERVICE_URL`, defaulting to `http://localhost:5009/api/connector-service`) via a dedicated axios instance, bypassing any Next.js API proxy, with a request interceptor (line 64) attaching `Authorization: Bearer <token>` — the token now sourced from the NextAuth session (`getSession()`, line 34) rather than Redux state, but the direct-to-connector-service-origin, proxy-bypassing pattern is unchanged.
**Re-verified 2026-08-27:** STILL OPEN, relocated from `GDriveFileBrowser.jsx` (no longer applicable — no raw fetch there) to `integrationHubService.js` (the real current location of the bearer-token-to-connector-service-origin pattern). NOTE: separately, the specific Google Drive routes this service calls do not even exist on the connector-service side — see new Critical defect EM-042, which supersedes this as the primary blocker for the Google Drive feature specifically (this defect's security concern still applies to every other integration-hub call routed through this same service file).
**2026-08-29 assessment:** Deliberately left unfixed after review with the user. There is no Next.js API proxy anywhere in this app to "bypass" — every backend call (including the main `vibrantix-backend`, not just connector-service) is made directly from the browser with a bearer token attached client-side; this is the app's established, deliberate calling convention, not a one-off mistake in this file. connector-service's CORS allowlist (`index.ts`) already includes the real prod/dev domains, so the "CORS failure likely in production" claim is not currently substantiated. Building an isolated proxy for just this one service would be architecturally inconsistent with the rest of the app and would not meaningfully reduce token exposure (the token still has to be usable by browser JS to attach to requests either way) — a real fix would mean session-based server-side auth across the whole app, a much larger initiative than a single-file patch. Left open pending a deliberate app-wide architecture decision, not scheduled as part of this fix pass.
**Claude Fix Prompt (original):**
```
1. Create a Next.js API route (e.g. app/api/integration-hub/[...path]/route.js) that proxies requests to CONNECTOR_SERVICE_URL server-side, attaching the bearer token from the server-side session rather than exposing it to a cross-origin client request.
2. In integrationHubService.js, replace the direct axios baseURL pointing at CONNECTOR_SERVICE_URL with calls to the new Next.js proxy route.
3. Remove NEXT_PUBLIC_CONNECTOR_SERVICE_URL (a client-exposed env var) once no client code calls the connector service directly.
```

title: Verdict rejection silently overwritten by next AI-upload callback
fixEvidence: First formally persisted to the JSON store this run (previously documented only in this agent's own 'Known Confirmed Defects' narrative, never written to a severity file). Verified FIXED in code as of 2026-08-27: `evidence-control-verdicts.controller.js:135-165` (`reportControlVerdicts`, the AI-upload 'completed' callback) still does a full-array replace of `evidence.controlVerdicts` (line 139: `evidenceUpdate.controlVerdicts = verdicts.map(...)`), but it now explicitly builds a `priorByCode` lookup (lines 135-137) and, for any `uclCode` whose prior `reviewStatus` was not `'pending'` (i.e. previously `'approved'` or `'rejected'`), carries forward `reviewStatus`/`reviewedBy`/`reviewedAt`/`rejectionReason` from the prior record instead of resetting to `'pending'` (lines 141, 157-162). An inline comment (lines 123-134) explicitly documents this as a deliberate fix for exactly this bug: "A human review decision must survive a re-run of the pipeline. This used to hard-code reviewStatus:'pending' for every incoming verdict...". Confirmed via `git log` that this file has received targeted fix commits. No dedicated regression test exists yet for this specific preserve-on-rerun behavior — worth adding, but the production code path is confirmed correct.
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/evidence/evidence.model.js` (`controlVerdicts[]` schema); `evidence-control-verdicts.controller.js` (AI-upload callback); `evidence-verdict-rejection.model.js` (append-only rejection log)
**Root Cause (original, as documented in this agent's architecture notes 2026-08-16):** Rejecting an AI-suggested control verdict flipped `evidence.controlVerdicts[].reviewStatus` to `'rejected'` in place, but the next AI-upload callback for that evidence item replaced the entire `controlVerdicts[]` array wholesale, silently discarding the rejection.
**Status:** FIXED — see fixEvidence. This record is being persisted to the JSON store for the first time in this run; it was previously described only in this agent's narrative documentation, never logged as a JSON defect.

title: Evidence can be uploaded and saved with zero requirement/control/UCL mapping, and nothing in the UI flags it as unmapped
description:
`createEvidence` (`vibrantix-backend/src/modules/evidence/evidence-upload.controller.js:343-551`) only requires `title`, `evidenceType`, and a file. `requirementMappings`/`directUclMappings` (lines 353-354) are optional and default to `[]`; if empty, no `EvidenceRequirementMapping`/`EvidenceUclMapping` row is ever written, yet the document is saved as real, filed evidence. Coverage is correctly computed only from evidence IDs already present in `ClientRequirement.evidenceIds`/`ClientControl.evidenceIds`, so unmapped evidence is correctly excluded from coverage math - but there is no compensating signal anywhere in the UI: `EvidenceTable.jsx` and the evidence-management component tree have no 'unmapped'/'no controls linked' badge or filter.

Auditor-facing breakage: an org can accumulate evidence that looks 'filed' in Evidence Management indefinitely with no control behind it, and nothing on the list screen tells the auditor which items these are.
requirement: ISO 27001:2022 Clause 7.5.2 documented information must indicate its nature

title: No true single-pane 'evidence by control across every source' view even within Evidence Management itself; two structurally separate mapping systems both partial
description:
The one control-centric evidence view in Evidence Management, `ControlDetailsDrawer.jsx:73-98`, calls only `evidenceService.getMappingsByControl(lookupId)`, which reads solely from the LEGACY `EvidenceControlMapping` collection. It does not query `EvidenceUclMapping`/`EvidenceRequirementMapping` (the newer, AI-verdict-fed system), nor integration evidence, cloud-posture, vendor, or policy evidence - those live on `ClientControl`'s separate `integrationEvidenceIds`/`vendorControlIds`/`policyIds`/`certificationIds`/`scannerCheckIds` arrays, which have no exposed aggregate read endpoint reachable from this drawer.

Auditor-facing breakage: two structurally separate evidence-mapping systems coexist, and the only 'view evidence for this control' screen in Evidence Management shows just one of them - an auditor picking a control here can be shown an incomplete evidence set while believing it's exhaustive.
